'''Chen Zhili''' ({{lang-zh|s=陈至立}}; born November 1942)<ref>{{cite web |url=http://news.xinhuanet.com/ziliao/2002-03/01/content_295698.htm |title=陈至立简历 |access-date=2009-12-29 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100927081255/http://news.xinhuanet.com/ziliao/2002-03/01/content_295698.htm |archive-date=2010-09-27 }}</ref> is a retired senior Chinese politician who served as [[State Councilor]] and [[Minister of Education (China)|Minister of Education]], and a [[Vice Chairperson of the National People's Congress|Vice Chairwoman of the National People's Congress]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Who's Who in China's Leadership |url=http://www.china.org.cn/english/features/58567.htm |access-date=2024-08-25 |website=www.china.org.cn}}</ref> She was also vice chairwoman of the organization commission of the [[2008 Beijing Olympics]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=State Councilor Meets Singaporean Education Minister -- china.org.cn |url=http://www.china.org.cn/english/education/189799.htm |access-date=2024-08-25 |website=www.china.org.cn}}</ref>

==Biography==
Born in [[Xianyou County]], [[Fujian|Fujian Province]], Chen graduated from the department of physics at [[Fudan University]]. She pursued her postgraduate degree at Shanghai Institute of Ceramics of [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]], doing research of solid-state physics. Chen joined the [[Chinese Communist Party]] ("CCP") in January 1961. At the beginning of the [[Cultural Revolution]], Chen was sent to work in an army farm for two years before returning to the Institute. In 1982, she was at [[Penn State University]] in the United States as a visiting scholar. After that, she was elevated to vice Party Chief of the Institute, and thus transformed from a scholar to a CCP official.

Chen's former posts in [[Shanghai]] included vice secretary and later, secretary of the CCP committee of Shanghai Science and Technology Commission, director of the Publicity Department of Shanghai, and vice secretary of CCP Shanghai committee. During her tenure in Shanghai, [[Jiang Zemin]], [[Zhu Rongji]], [[Wu Bangguo]] and [[Huang Ju]] served as Shanghai's Party chief.{{citation needed|date=October 2012}}

In August 1997, Chen was transferred to central government and appointed as vice director and leader of Party group of National Education Commission. In 1998, she became the Minister of Education.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Who's Who |url=http://edition.cnn.com/ASIANOW/asiaweek/magazine/99/0924/voc50people/content/chen.zhili.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240825130731/http://edition.cnn.com/ASIANOW/asiaweek/magazine/99/0924/voc50people/content/chen.zhili.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=August 25, 2024 |access-date=2024-08-25 |website=CNN}}</ref> In 2003, she was further elevated to the position of [[State Councilor]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=State Councilor visits CAS Institute of Geochemistry----Chinese Academy of Sciences |url=https://english.cas.cn/newsroom/archive/china_archive/cn2004/200909/t20090923_40751.shtml |access-date=2024-08-25 |website=english.cas.cn}}</ref> in charge of education, culture and sports. In March 2008, Chen was elected a [[Vice Chairperson of the National People's Congress]]. On April 12, 2008, she was appointed as governor of Beijing Olympic Village.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2008-07-27 |title=Beijing's Olympic village opens |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/asia-pacific/7527446.stm |access-date=2024-08-25 |language=en-GB}}</ref>

Chen was an alternate member of [[13th Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party|13th]] and [[14th Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party|14th]] Central Committees of the Chinese Communist Party, and a full member of [[15th Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party|15th]], [[16th Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party|16th]], [[17th Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party|17th]] Central Committees.
